newsitem.title: UK: BTP says profits rise, sees further growth.
newsitem.headline: BTP says profits rise, sees further growth.

text.p: British chemicals group BTP Plc, posting a rise in annual profits, said on Tuesday it expected further growth at its divisions this year despite the impact of sterling's strength.
BTP's pre-tax profits rose 8.0 percent to 48.2 million pounds ($78.8 million) in the year to March 31, excluding exceptional charges in the year-ago figures.
The company said strong sterling hurt profits in the second half by about 3.0 million pounds.

"Whilst the worst effects are over, this will continue to be a feature as we enter 1997/98. However, the opportunities that exist across the group should ensure we enjoy a period of continued growth," chief executive Steve Hannam said in BTP's earnings statement.
He added that most of last year's growth was organic, with investment in new equipment and products expected to produce volume growth and yield added benefits this year.
BTP also said it named Ken Greatbatch as its new finance director after Rob Martin resigned from the post.
Greatbatch was previously chief executive at Laporte Australia Ltd, in addition to holding other positions at Laporte Plc, a speciality chemicals firm. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
